title: Esther 7
paragraphs: ¹ So the king and Haman went to dine with Queen Esther. ² On this second day, as they were drinking wine, the king again asked Esther, "What is your petition, Queen Esther? It will be granted. What is your request? Even up to half the kingdom, it will be done." ³ Then Queen Esther answered, "If I have found favor in your sight, O king, and if it pleases the king, let my life be spared at my petition, and my people at my request. ⁴ For my people and I have been sold to be destroyed, killed, and annihilated. If we had merely been sold as male and female slaves, I would have stayed quiet, since that trouble would not have been worth troubling the king." ⁵ King Ahasuerus asked Queen Esther, "Who is he? Where is the man who has dared to do such a thing?"

⁶ Esther said, "The adversary and enemy is this wicked Haman." Haman was terrified before the king and queen. ⁷ The king got up in a rage and went into the palace garden, while Haman stayed behind to beg Queen Esther for his life, because he could see that the king had already decided to destroy him. ⁸ When the king returned from the palace garden to the banqueting hall, Haman had thrown himself onto the couch where Esther was reclining. "Will he even assault the queen right here in my own palace?" the king burst out. The moment those words left his mouth, the servants covered Haman's face. ⁹ Then Harbonah, one of the eunuchs attending the king, said, "A gallows seventy-five feet high is standing at Haman's house — the very one Haman had built for Mordecai, who spoke up to help the king." "Hang him on it!" the king commanded. ¹⁰ So they hanged Haman on the gallows he had built for Mordecai, and the king's fury subsided.
